title: Evaluating a Deterministic Validator Plus Single‑Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=300 paired intent→configuration tasks; preregistration id cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1, preregistration SHA-256 archived) to evaluate whether a minimal guarded pipeline—single‑shot LLM generation (declared model: gpt-5-mini) followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to plain single‑shot generation. Execution completed 600 episodes and used 301 model calls. Observed outcomes: baseline = 299/300 valid (99.667%); guarded = 300/300 valid (100.0%); paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single permitted automated repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1; Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]). The preregistered planning assumption used for power calculations (planned baseline pass rate = 0.40) was contradicted by the observed near‑ceiling baseline, removing statistical headroom for the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction target. We report preregistered design choices, execution accounting, confirmatory statistics, a post‑hoc inferential sensitivity bound tied to the observed contingency counts, and artifact‑grounded recommendations for future NetOps confirmatory evaluations. All run artifacts and analysis outputs are archived in the execution manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Operator intent translation to device configuration is a central NetOps activity. Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate intent→configuration workflows, but probabilistic generation introduces misordering, omission, and unsafe commands. Recent literature recommends guarded architectures that pair LLM generators with deterministic validators and bounded repair loops to reduce operational risk [10.1002/nem.2313, 10.36227/techrxiv.176784505.56675782/v1]. However, preregistered, artifact‑grounded evaluations that quantify the incremental effect of tightly bounded guardrails on first‑pass misconfiguration rates are limited. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to test whether a minimal guarded pipeline—a single shared LLM candidate per task, a frozen deterministic validator, and at most one automated repair call—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to single‑shot generation. Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experiment with deterministic seed generation and archived per‑task artifacts; (2) confirmatory inference and exact artifact‑grounded contingency counts; (3) a post‑hoc sensitivity bound tied to observed discordant counts; (4) concrete, artifact‑grounded design recommendations for follow‑on confirmatory NetOps studies.
sections.related_work: LLM‑driven intent translation and configuration synthesis have been demonstrated in lab and testbed settings with promising results but documented failure modes (omission, ordering errors, overconfidence) that threaten operational safety [10.1002/nem.2313]. Work in adjacent domains (medical QA, code repair) demonstrates that verifier‑assisted and retrieval‑augmented pipelines can reduce factual errors and improve grounding, motivating similar guarded patterns for NetOps [10.36227/techrxiv.176784505.56675782/v1, 10.2139/ssrn.6608518]. Deterministic network verification techniques (header‑space analysis, specification checking) provide algorithmic bases for validators that statically check reachability and policy constraints without live execution [10.1145/3098822.3098834]. Surveys and policy documents emphasize generate→verify→repair architectures and highlight auditability, provenance, and human‑oversight concerns as open deployment challenges [10.6028/nist.ai.100-2e2023]. Our study situates itself at the intersection of these strands by producing an artifact‑anchored confirmatory comparison of single‑shot generation versus validator+single‑iteration repair.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: The experiment was preregistered (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) prior to observing outcomes; the preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest. Design: paired within‑task sampling using a deterministic task generator produced 300 seeds; each seed yielded a single shared LLM candidate that served as the baseline response and as the starting point for the guarded arm (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Planned episodes = 600 (two episodes per seed); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Generator and execution policy: declared model = gpt-5-mini; execution accounting limited total model calls to ≤600. The authoritative recorded model configuration is execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). That artifact records the model declaration and the sampling parameter: execution/model_configuration.json records "temperature": null. A null/unset temperature value is not evidence of deterministic sampling (temperature=0); sampling determinism therefore remains unspecified in the archived run and is a design factor that can affect generator variance and power planning. Validator and scoring: the frozen deterministic validator canonicalized generated configurations to a normalized AST and applied full intent‑constraint validation (required_sequence, expected_final_state, workflow policies such as must_be_down_for_fields and minimum_active_in_groups). The validator emitted structured traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, normalized_configuration, valid flag) used to trigger the single automated repair attempt and to compute per‑task scores. Repair adapter: invoked only when the validator reported violations on the shared candidate; repair was restricted to one automated attempt per episode and aimed at minimal edits to resolve reported violations. Primary estimand and test: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; exact McNemar two‑sided test at α=0.05; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Contamination and exclusions: preregistered deterministic AST equality and near‑duplicate checks; any exact duplicates would be deterministically excluded and replaced from a preregistered reserve set. Reproducibility primitives (task seeds, validator rules, repair prompt templates, analysis code) were archived in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact‑derived): planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 600; complete pairs analyzed = 300. Model calls used = 301 (300 shared initial generations + 1 repair invocation). No provider/infrastructure failures occurred under the preregistered retry policy; no deterministic contamination exclusions were applied. Primary outcomes (archived counts): baseline_success_count = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded_success_count = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency (guarded vs baseline): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Inferential results (preregistered): exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 1/300 ≈ 0.0033333. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Repair outcomes (H2): single allowed repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1); Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]. Post‑hoc sensitivity bound: the observed discordant count (n10 + n01 = 1) imposes a hard limit on resolvable absolute paired difference equal to 1/300 ≈ 0.00333; the preregistered target (≥50% relative reduction from a planned baseline of 0.40) would have required ~90 net discordant pairs favoring guarded outputs and therefore could not be detected given the observed near‑ceiling baseline. Representative per‑task validator traces and repair prompts/responses for every episode are archived in the execution bundle and are the authoritative source for the reported counts.
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded interpretation: the archived contingency (n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0) directly constrains inference—the paired difference equals (n10 − n01)/N = 1/300, and McNemar conditioning on the single discordant pair yields p = 1.00. The preregistered planning assumption (baseline pass rate = 0.40) largely determined sample‑size calculations; the observed baseline (0.9967) eliminated statistical headroom to detect the preregistered large relative effect. Design tradeoffs: the shared_initial_candidate pairing emulates operational workflows where a single plan is reviewed and repaired, improving ecological validity for remediation claims but increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing expected discordant pairs. Consequently, study designers who expect to evaluate repair effectiveness should either calibrate task difficulty to ensure a nontrivial initial failure prevalence or adopt an independent‑draws design if the operational question targets marginal generator differences. Validator traces: deterministic canonicalization and structured violation codes enable precise failure‑mode diagnosis (syntax/canonicalization mismatch, missing commands, dependency‑order violations, protected‑field touches) and support reproducible post‑mortems; these traces were essential to identify and repair the single failing candidate. Construct validity: our validator performed static canonicalization and rule checking rather than dynamic emulation of runtime semantics (control‑plane convergence, transient reachability); therefore, the results are conditional on the validator's static semantics and do not measure runtime behavior. Sampling determinism caveat: the archived model_configuration.json records "temperature": null (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Because null does not equal a fixed zero temperature, sampling determinism was unspecified and generator variance could differ if runs were repeated with explicit temperature settings. Operational implication: when baseline error is rare, a validator+bounded repair pipeline primarily serves as a safety net for rare mistakes rather than as a throughput booster; evaluation goals (error reduction vs catastrophic‑risk mitigation) should guide task bank selection, pairing semantics, and whether to include emulation stages.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=300 pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini) to a guarded pipeline composed of a frozen deterministic validator and a single automated repair iteration. Baseline generation produced 299/300 valid outputs and the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs; the single repair corrected the lone invalid baseline output. The observed near‑ceiling baseline contradicted the preregistered planning assumption (baseline pass rate = 0.40), removing the statistical headroom required to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction. Future confirmatory NetOps studies should (1) calibrate task difficulty or adversarially augment tasks to obtain a targeted number of initial failures or discordant pairs, (2) preregister pairing semantics and repair budgets and incorporate their effect on discordant counts into power calculations, and (3) include emulation/simulation when runtime semantic consequences are part of the operational claim. All raw outputs, validator traces, repair traces, the execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived and enumerated in the Disclosure Statement for independent verification.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor‑template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

The preregistered power plan assumed a baseline pass rate = 0.40; the observed baseline (299/300) contradicted that assumption and removed headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction.
Sampling semantics (shared_initial_candidate) reused the same initial candidate across paired arms, increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing discordant pairs available to McNemar inference.

Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; actual runtime consequences of configurations were not executed and remain unmeasured.

H2 repair‑success evidence is based on a single initially invalid case (1/1 → 100%), yielding a wide Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]; larger counts of initial failures are required to estimate repair effectiveness precisely.

The archived model_configuration.json records "temperature": null (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa); because null does not equal an explicit zero temperature, sampling determinism was unspecified and could affect repeatability and generator variance in replicated studies.
